Help
Using CompassIQ

CompassIQ builds your quarter call plan around where your doctors are, how often each one should be seen, and when their offices are open. Everything you do is saved on this device automatically. Five steps take you from a new territory to today's route.

  1. Load your territoryGo to Settings → Territory setup, choose your territory and select Load territory.
  2. Set your home ZIPIn Settings, enter your 5-digit home ZIP and select Calculate travel times. Every drive time and route starts from here.
  3. Set hours and time offIn Settings, confirm work hours and daily call target, and add PTO, half days and company holidays.
  4. Build your planGo to Plan → Build plan, set the quarter start date (a Monday) and label, review Capacity analysis, then select Build my plan.
  5. Work from DriveEach morning, open Drive for today's stops in order, the route map and directions. Adjust the schedule any time under Plan → Schedule.

Where things are

DriveToday's route: stops in order, drive time, route map, directions, Out today and Add meal.
EngageYour doctor list. Select a doctor to set office hours, other locations, meals and routing rules.
PlanSchedule: the quarter calendar, by week or month. Build plan: generate or regenerate the quarter.
TrackTerritory: route KPIs and the territory map. Summary: plan metrics. Plan health: score and alerts.
MapAny day's or week's route, or every doctor in the territory.
ReportsDaily itinerary, Outlook calendar, Excel, CSV, Salesforce file, quarter summary and R&F report.
SettingsTerritory, home ZIP, hours, time off, prescribing trends, and Data & Backup.
On iPad portraitThe menu moves to tabs along the bottom; Reports, Settings, Find and Help are under More.
Find a doctorSearch box at the top of the menu (⌘K / Ctrl+K on a keyboard).
Save backupBottom of the menu. Downloads a copy of your plan; the status line shows when it last saved on this device.
Compliance: CompassIQ is a routing and scheduling tool only. Log every call in your company CRM as required.

Drive

  • Opens on today: the number of stops, total drive time, and how this week and quarter are pacing.
  • The Next stop card shows who is next, when, and the drive from your last stop. Directions opens Apple Maps; Done moves you to the following stop; Missed records a reason so the doctor can be rescheduled. Log every call in your CRM as well.
  • Use ‹ / Next day › to look ahead, and Edit route to see the day on the map.
  • Today's route lists each stop with its time, drive from the previous stop, segment and any meal. Select a stop to open that doctor's preferences; Directions opens Apple Maps.
  • The route map shows home, each stop numbered in visit order and colored by segment, and meals ringed in amber.
  • Out today marks today as time off and moves today's calls into upcoming days. Add meal books a meal or appointment in a few taps.
  • On iPad, the microphone button takes short voice commands — "I'm out today", "PTO Monday through Friday", "Lunch with Dr. Chen Tuesday at noon". Nothing changes until you confirm.
  • The next workday card shows your first and last stop, skipping weekends and time off.

Engage — doctors & preferences

  • Search, or use the quick filters — Trend flagged, New writers, Not visited yet, Segment A. Each doctor shows segment, call goal, planned calls and the next scheduled visit.
  • Select a doctor to open Scheduling preferences:
    • Hours & locations — untick days the office is closed, set office hours, add a preferred visit window, or add a different location for a specific day.
    • Meals & appts — book a breakfast, lunch, snack or appointment on a date. Times fill in by type.
    • Routing rules — Do not call, By appointment only, or New HCP.
  • Saving a change that affects scheduling (hours, meals, Do not call, appointment only) updates the plan automatically.

Plan — Schedule

  • Week view shows five day columns with call times, segment colors and drive times. Month view shows the whole quarter with meals highlighted.
  • Move a call: drag it to another position or day (on iPad, press and hold, then tap the target day). Times recalculate automatically.
  • Move a whole day: in Month view, drag the day to another date. Dropping on a day with calls swaps the two days.
  • Lock a day with ✅ on the day header once it's done. Locked days are never changed by regeneration. Unlock with 🔓.
  • Break block: drag it onto a day to reserve time; calls reschedule around it.
  • Remove a call with ✕. An amber banner offers Add to routing to bring that doctor back into the plan.
  • Tap a visit to mark it done or missed, open the doctor, get directions, see the day on the map, or remove it. Missed calls can be rescheduled from the banner at the top of the calendar.
  • Overnight stays: a purple banner appears when the drive to the first call is longer than your overnight threshold (2 hours by default). Select it to add a hotel; the next day's calls re-cluster around the hotel.
  • Daily itinerary prints day-by-day call sheets.

Plan — Build plan

  • Set the first day (a Monday) and last day of the plan. The last day defaults to the end of the quarter.
  • Partial quarters are prorated: if the plan covers less than the full quarter (for example, starting in November), each doctor's call goal is scaled to the share of working days covered — e.g. 7 calls becomes 5 for a plan covering 65% of the quarter. Every doctor keeps at least one call; trend extras are added on top.
  • Pre-flight checks confirm doctors are loaded, travel times exist and the start date is valid.
  • Capacity analysis compares the calls needed with the slots available. If the quarter is short, the planner first raises the daily target (up to 30), then trims C and D frequencies so every doctor still gets at least one visit.
  • Build my plan builds the schedule in seconds. Regenerating keeps locked days, meals, hotel stays, time off and doctor preferences.
  • A yellow Plan may be outdated banner means the routing engine has improved since your plan was built. Regenerate to apply it.

Track

  • Territory — route KPIs and the territory map:
    • Avg calls/day — planned calls ÷ working days.
    • Avg drive-in — minutes from home (or hotel) to the first call.
    • Avg between calls — minutes between consecutive stops.
    • Drive per day — all driving on a workday, including the drive-in, with the quarter total.
    • HCP reach — share of callable doctors who appear in the plan.
    • The map plots every doctor by segment, plus your home.
  • Summary — total calls, working days, efficiency score, drive hours, co-located calls and time allocation.
  • Plan health — an overall score with findings, such as days under target or days that may feel rushed.

Map

  • Day shows one day's route with numbered stops. Week shows each day in its own color. Use ◀ ▶ to step through.
  • A dashed line is the drive-in from home or a hotel; solid lines connect calls in order.
  • All HCPs plots the whole territory.

Reports

  • Outlook calendar — adds your plan to Outlook as its own calendar, so it can be removed in one step. See the FAQ for import steps.
  • Daily itinerary — printable day sheets with addresses, times and meals.
  • Excel workbook — calendar, doctor list and ZIP4 zones on separate sheets.
  • Calendar CSV — every call with all fields.
  • Salesforce export — CSV with CRM field names for Data Loader.
  • Quarter summary and Reach & Frequency report — printable summaries of coverage and frequency attainment.

Settings

  • Territory setup — choose and load your territory, set your home ZIP and calculate travel times.
  • Prescribing trends — load an HCP-level trend file to adjust routing. The template has columns NPI, Trend, L13W_TRx, Prior_TRx, Pct_Change and Note; Trend is New writer, Grower, Decliner, Lapsed or Stable. Default rules:
    • New writers get 2 extra calls with a first visit by week 3.
    • Decliners and lapsed writers get 1 extra call with a first visit by week 6.
    • Flagged doctors are trimmed last if the quarter runs short.
    • You can change the numbers; they apply the next time you build the plan.
  • Work hours & targets — workday start and end, daily target, appointment length, buffer between stops and an optional daily break.
  • Travel & overnight — drive-time calculation, overnight threshold and how each day starts (nearest or farthest first).
  • Time off & holidays — full and half days off. Current-year US holidays are pre-loaded.
  • Data & Backup — save or load a backup file, and move your data into a new version.

How the routing engine works

  • Frequency: each doctor's annual call goal becomes a quarterly count, spread evenly across the 13 weeks.
  • Geography: doctors are grouped by ZIP4 zone. Each day works the highest-demand nearby zone and avoids repeating the same area on back-to-back days.
  • Priority: Segment A before B, C and D within each day. A and B doctors more than two weeks overdue get extra priority.
  • Same office: doctors at the same address are visited together, and an office is visited at most once a week.
  • Start times: the first call allows for the drive from home or the previous night's hotel.
  • Sweep weeks: for zones more than about 140 minutes from home, the engine plans whole weeks in that region with hotel-to-hotel days instead of daily round trips.
  • Trends: if a trend file is loaded, flagged doctors get the extra calls and earlier first visits described in Settings.

Saving & versions

Is my work saved automatically?

Yes. Every change saves to this device's browser as you work, and it stays there when you close the app or restart the iPad. The status under Save backup in the menu shows the last save. If it turns red and reads Not saved, the browser's storage is full — select Save backup right away.

Why should I also use Save backup?

Browser storage belongs to one device and one browser. Clearing browser data, a new iPad or a different browser starts empty. Save backup downloads a copy you can reload from Settings → Data & Backup → Load backup. A reminder appears if you haven't backed up in 7 days.

A new version of CompassIQ was released. Will I lose my plan?

Not on the same device and link — your plan, preferences and edits carry over. Before switching to a different file or device, go to Settings → Data & Backup → Step 1 — Export my data, then import that file into the new version with Step 2 — Import into new version.

Scheduling & routing

I changed a doctor's hours or added a meal. Does the plan update?

Yes. Changes that affect scheduling — office hours, meals, Do not call, appointment only — regenerate the plan automatically, and a message confirms it. Preferred windows and the New HCP flag save without regenerating; they apply the next time you build the plan.

Will regenerating change days I've already locked?

No. Locked days are excluded from regeneration and kept exactly as they are. The plan is rebuilt around them.

Why doesn't the plan reach every doctor at full frequency?

The quarter doesn't have enough call slots. The planner raises the daily target first (up to 30), then trims D and C frequencies so every doctor gets at least one visit. Plan → Build plan → Capacity analysis shows the gap and has a one-click fix to raise your daily target.

Are doctors at the same address visited together?

Yes. Doctors at the same address are treated as one office and scheduled back to back, and an office is visited at most once a week. The exception is a doctor whose hours only allow a different day.

I removed a call with ✕. Can I get that doctor back?

Yes. The amber banner at the top of Plan → Schedule lists removed doctors. Add to routing puts them back into the earliest open slots; Dismiss leaves them out.

What's the difference between office hours and a preferred window?

Office hours are fixed — the planner never schedules a doctor on a closed day or outside their hours. A preferred window is a preference the planner follows when it can.

Do not call vs. By appointment only?

Do not call removes the doctor from routing entirely. By appointment only keeps them in the plan only on dates you book under Meals & appts.

Will a booked meal always stay in the plan?

Yes. Meals and appointments are pinned to their date and time. The planner also holds that doctor out of routing for the 3 days before, so you don't visit twice that week.

How do prescribing trends change my plan?

When a trend file is loaded under Settings → Prescribing trends, flagged doctors get extra calls and an earlier first visit (by default, new writers +2 calls by week 3; decliners and lapsed writers +1 call by week 6). Rebuild the plan to apply a new file. The first visit is pulled earlier but still grouped with nearby doctors, so it can land a week or so after the target.

Travel & overnights

How are drive times calculated?

From your home ZIP to each doctor's ZIP, using road-network times where available and a distance-based estimate otherwise (35 mph local, 55 mph under 80 miles, 65 mph beyond). Select Calculate travel times in Settings after changing your home ZIP.

When should I add an overnight stay?

When the purple Overnight suggested banner appears on a day in Plan → Schedule — the drive to the first call is longer than your threshold (2 hours by default). Select the banner to add the hotel.

What is a sweep week?

For doctors far from home, the planner groups those calls into dedicated weeks: drive out Monday, work the area hotel to hotel, and head home Friday. This replaces repeated day-long round trips and typically saves several call days of driving each quarter. Sweep weeks are chosen automatically; you can shift them by moving whole days in Month view.

I switched territories and drive times look wrong.

Loading a new territory clears the home ZIP, travel times and hotel stays. Re-enter your home ZIP in Settings and select Calculate travel times.

Outlook & exports

How do I add my plan to Outlook without cluttering my calendar?

Reports → Outlook calendar → Send to Outlook. Import the file into its own calendar:

  • New Outlook / Outlook on the web: Calendar → Add calendar → Create blank calendar (e.g. "CompassIQ Q4 2026"), then Upload from file into that calendar.
  • Classic Outlook: File → Open & Export → Import/Export → Import an iCalendar (.ics) → Open as New.

Don't double-click the file — that merges every visit into your main calendar. Exporting from today forward is recommended.

How do I remove a plan from Outlook?

If you imported into its own calendar, right-click that calendar → Delete calendar. If visits went into your main calendar, switch to List view, filter by the category CompassIQ, select all and delete. For older imports without that category, use Download "remove from Outlook" file in the Outlook dialog and open it in Outlook.

Can I see a whole week's route on the map?

Yes. In Map, switch to Week. Each day has its own color; use ◀ ▶ to step through weeks.
